title: LWCal: Loss-Weighted Calibration for Tabular Classifiers with Noisy Calibration Labels
LWCAL: Loss-Weighted Calibration for Tabular Classifiers with Noisy Calibration Labels
summary: The paper studies post-hoc probability calibration for tabular classifiers when the held-out calibration labels are noisy, which breaks the clean-calibration-label assumption of Platt, isotonic, and beta calibration. It proposes LWCAL, a CPU-only weighted isotonic calibrator that down-weights calibration points by a median/MAD-normalized noisy-label loss, and GATED-LWCAL, which backs off toward raw scores when apparent label-model contradiction is high. In the 432-cell random-forest study, GATED-LWCAL reduces mean ECE from 0.188 to 0.122 and NLL from 0.438 to 0.396, while pure LWCAL achieves the lowest ECE at 0.113.

"""One-off helper: back up the authors' pristine cached CSVs (git HEAD) into
REPRO_DATA_CACHE and restore repo/data to the committed state, since the author
script overwrites the CSVs in place on every run."""
import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

cache = Path(os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "paper_cache"))
dest = cache / "lwcal_git_head_data"
dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

files = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "-C", "repo", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "HEAD", "data/"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
).stdout.split()

for rel in files:
    blob = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", "repo", "show", f"HEAD:{rel}"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout
    (dest / Path(rel).name).write_text(blob, encoding="utf-8")
    print("backed up", rel, len(blob), "chars")

# restore working tree data to committed (pristine paper) state
subprocess.run(["git", "-C", "repo", "checkout", "--", "data/"], check=True)
subprocess.run(["git", "-C", "repo", "checkout", "--", "requirements.txt", "environment.json"], check=True)
print("restored repo/data to git HEAD")

"""Reproduce the LWCAL paper's main random-forest result (Table III / claim C1).

Pipeline
--------

   6 seeds x 2 noise modes x 5 noise rates and writes ``repo/data/*.csv``.
2. Load the regenerated ``repo/data/main_results.csv``, keep the noisy cells
   (noise_rate > 0, i.e. the 432 cells excluding the clean eta=0 rows), and
   average ECE / NLL / Brier per calibration method with equal weight per cell.
3. Cross-check the other Table III / Table V aggregates (claims C2-C8) and the

4. Optionally log per-cell m, s, d_hat, rho and the calibration weights
   (requirement R13) using the authors' own functions, for auditability.
5. Write ``results/metrics.json``.

The expected target values below come from the claim contract (state/
claim_contract.json) and are used ONLY for the pass/fail comparison; every

def run_author_script(timeout_s: float) -> dict:
    cmd = [sys.executable, "scripts/trimcal_eval.py", "--skip-compile"]
    print(f"[reproduce] running author experiment: {' '.join(cmd)} (cwd={REPO})")
    t0 = time.time()

        cwd=str(REPO),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,

"""Cheap determinism check: recompute one experiment cell (breast_cancer, seed 11,
symmetric, eta=0.2) with the authors' functions and compare ECE/NLL/Brier of every
calibration method to the values in the freshly regenerated repo/data/main_results.csv."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "repo" / "scripts"))
import trimcal_eval as te

row_filter = dict(dataset="breast_cancer", seed=11, noise_mode="symmetric", noise_rate=0.2)
csv = pd.read_csv(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "repo" / "data" / "main_results.csv")
csv = csv[(csv["experiment"] == "main") & (csv["dataset"] == row_filter["dataset"]) &
          (csv["seed"] == row_filter["seed"]) & (csv["noise_mode"] == row_filter["noise_mode"]) &
          (np.isclose(csv["noise_rate"], row_filter["noise_rate"]))]
print("csv rows for cell:", len(csv))

data = [d for d in te.make_datasets() if d.name == "breast_cancer"][0]
seed = row_filter["seed"]
X_train, X_cal, X_test, y_train, y_cal, y_test = te.split_data(data.X, data.y, seed)
noise_seed = seed * 10000 + 200 + 0  # symmetric -> +0
y_train_noisy = te.corrupt_labels(y_train, 0.2, "symmetric", noise_seed)
y_cal_noisy = te.corrupt_labels(y_cal, 0.2, "symmetric", noise_seed + 333)
model = te.rf_model(seed)
model.fit(X_train, y_train_noisy)
p_cal, p_test = te.proba_pos(model, X_cal), te.proba_pos(model, X_test)

ok = True
for method, p_eval in te.calibration_methods(p_cal, y_cal_noisy, p_test).items():
    m = te.eval_metrics(y_test, p_eval)
    got = csv[csv["method"] == method].iloc[0]
    for metric in ["ece", "nll", "brier"]:
        match = np.isclose(m[metric], float(got[metric]), rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        ok &= match
        print(f"{method:>12s} {metric:>6s}: recomputed={m[metric]:.12f} csv={float(got[metric]):.12f} match={match}")
print("DETERMINISM CHECK:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
